caseDevelopment.html:
The Ancog family was checked using the Family Risk and Vulnerability Assessment (FRVA). The results showed they have low risk in finances and the environment, and no risks in health, safety, or protecting children.
Their latest Social Welfare and Development Indicator (SWDI) assessment was done on October 10, 2025. It showed their family’s income is at Level 2, meaning they just meet basic needs (subsistence level). Their average monthly income per person is Php1,713.33. The poverty line in Bohol is Php2,170.74 per person each month, and the average food cost in the province is Php1,515.83.
The family has four more years to be in the program basing on the 7-year limit R.A 11310 and since they are still legible for the program due to their three children Nico, Tito Jr. and Blessy.
Edna is a 43-year-old grantee who has been a partner-beneficiary of the Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program (4Ps) for two years. Their main concern is the family’s insufficient income coming from unstable type of work and only her husband making for a living, which makes it difficult for them to cover essential needs such as healthcare and education for their children Nico, Tito Jr. and Blessy. This situation has continued over time, mainly due to their limited sources of income where Edna only assists her husband depending on the season of selling harvested root crops and vegetables. While her husband, Tito, works as a farmer. Based on the latest Social Welfare and Development Indicator (SWDI), their family is at level 2 (Subsistence Level). Their combined earnings are just enough to meet basic needs, with an average monthly income per person of Php1,713.33, which is below the poverty line which resulted insufficient to comfortably afford health and educational expenses. With the rising health and education costs have put a real strain on their finances. Plus, living on a remote Barangay and relying only on farming, which is easily get affected by weather and environmental condition, it poses burden in terms of family’s finances. The Ancog family have been struggling for a while but this burden was unloaded through the aid of the program; but things are getting more pressing now that their children Nico, Tito Jr. and Blessy must continue in their studies which needs increasing financial demands of supporting such as their school expenses such as food, school supplies, allowances, and other educational needs.
The family’s situation is not entirely permanent. The family may have big problems which mainly comes from social and economic issues that can be solve with the right help, support, and community programs. Ancog family is resilient, and they're involved in their community, which shows they want to change and improve for their family. Edna, in particular, has demonstrated her hardworking nature and willingness to seek solutions, which suggests that with appropriate support given, positive change is achievable.
Their environment also offers some available resources that can promote improvement. Local government programs which facilitate waste management, health services, and possible livelihood initiatives. The community has also basic facilities such as a health station, barangay hall, and water refilling stations, which can support health and sanitation needs. details.recommendationText: Edna and her family show resilience and are actively involved in their community, which are important strengths to build on. Their main livelihood activities like farming and selling own grown harvested root crops and vegetables are affected by seasonal weather and environmental factors, making their income unstable. They have good knowledge of health, safety, and disaster preparedness, but they need help in finding ways to diversify their income sources. Their strong social connections and participation in local groups provide a good foundation for receiving more support and making progress.
